week9/gradient_descent_fit.mp4:
## Video content

Duration: 10.0 seconds. The file has no audio track. The description is based on six evenly spaced frame samples through the video; it is a visual summary, not a transcription of every frame or a new experiment.

The animation shows the fitting of f(x) = a*x + b. The left panel shows BMI as standardised input and disease progression as the target. Red points are training data, blue triangles are validation data, and a red line is the current fit. The validation points are hidden at first and shown later; the caption states val revealed after iteration 250.

The right panel shows training loss and validation loss over iterations with MSE on a standardised scale. The line changes and the loss curves approach stable levels. The point is to distinguish between the training parameter updates and evaluation on held-out data. No exact final score was read or is reported here.
week9/kfold_fit_evolution_dual_init.mp4:
## Video content

Duration: 10.0 seconds. The file has no audio track. The description is based on six evenly spaced frame samples; it is a visual summary and not a transcription of every frame.

The left panel is titled Two Parallel Fits per Fold: Init A (solid) vs. Init B (dashed). It shows BMI as standardised input, disease progression as the target and five coloured folds. Init A starts as a horizontal line around the mean; Init B has a different starting value. Dashed and solid lines change through the iterations and approach each other.

The right panel is titled Mean Loss Across Folds (log scale). It shows training and validation loss for the two initialisations. One initialisation starts with a larger loss, but the curves fall and approach similar levels. The animation illustrates differences between initialisation and validation across folds. It is not evidence that all models always converge to the same solution.
week9/cnn_3letter_mixed_scripts.mp4:
## Video content

Duration: 12.6 seconds. The file has no audio track. The description is based on six evenly spaced frame samples; it is a visual summary and not a frame-by-frame transcription.

The animation shows a convolutional neural network (CNN) that receives a small image with three characters from different writing systems. The diagram is labelled Input: 3 letters, Conv 1 kernels + 4 maps, Conv 2 8 maps and 3 softmax heads. Three output heads correspond to the character positions.

At the top, training step, loss per letter, letter accuracy and triple accuracy are shown. On the right, the inferred characters and a loss indicator are shown; the true characters appear below them. Across the samples the input, activations and predictions change. The animation illustrates feature maps, multiple output heads and the difference between per-character and per-triple accuracy. The training figures shown are not an independent test measurement and are not used as new experimental results in StudyGraph.
